negative_findings.description: No evidence surfaced of a recent (post-2008) full IMF/World Bank FSAP or FSSA for North Macedonia. Search results referenced the 2003 FSAP and the 2008 FSAP Update with Basel Core Principles and stress-testing technical notes, but no newer cycle.
negative_findings.result_summary: Only historic FSAP material located; no announcement of a scheduled new MK FSAP found in this pass.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: The cell rationale assumed FSAP material as a pillar; if the latest assessment is ~2008, Article IV staff reports and the EC enlargement report carry more current supervisory assessment weight.

negative_findings.description: No dedicated North Macedonia module was found for global regulatory-tracker vendors (Thomson Reuters Regulatory Intelligence, Wolters Kluwer, Corlytics, CUBE) in open search; such coverage, if it exists, sits entirely behind sales walls.
negative_findings.result_summary: Vendor trackers could not be confirmed to cover MK at country granularity.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Means the commercial-tracker leg of this cell is unverified and may need direct vendor enquiry rather than open-web monitoring.

negative_findings.description: Attempts to locate a Moody's-published North Macedonia banking-sector outlook returned nothing specific; only Fitch sovereign material surfaced for MK.
negative_findings.result_summary: Fitch confirmed as an active MK sovereign rater; Moody's MK banking coverage not evidenced.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Avoids assuming a second rating-agency data stream that may not exist for this market.

negative_findings.description: The Macedonian-language search performed (mandatory local-language pass) returned overwhelmingly national primary sources — NBRNM law pages, Ministry of Finance portal PDFs, commercial-bank customer notices, Chamber of Commerce draft-law files — rather than English cross-border aggregators. No MK-language law-firm legal-bulletin service was identified in this pass.
negative_findings.result_summary: Local-language query surfaced primary/national sources belonging to other coverage cells, plus one useful government mirror of Fitch reports.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Confirms this cell is genuinely English-dominant, but also that MK-language law-firm newsletters are an unmapped gap; the mchamber.mk draft-law PDF hints at a consultation-tracking route worth handing to the national-sources cell.

negative_findings.description: Several high-value monitors are paywalled or registration-gated: SeeNews, bne IntelliNews, Central Banking, Mondaq, Lexology and Fitch's own portal.
negative_findings.result_summary: Headline-level monitoring is feasible; full-text collection requires subscriptions.
negative_findings.why_it_matters: Budget and ToS constraints shape what can be automated versus what must be manual or licensed.

coverage_gaps.description: Commercial regulatory-tracker vendors with confirmed North Macedonia coverage remain unidentified.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Contact Thomson Reuters Regulatory Intelligence, Corlytics, CUBE and Wolters Kluwer directly to confirm MK jurisdiction coverage and horizon-scanning depth before assuming a gap is permanent.

coverage_gaps.description: Local Skopje-based firms' own newsletters (e.g. Debarliev Dameski & Kelesoska, Polenak, Mens Legis, Lalicic & Partners, ODI Skopje) were only partially probed; their direct subscription feeds are likely faster than the aggregators that republish them.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Enumerate the top 8-10 MK banking/finance firms from Chambers, Legal 500 and CEE Legal Matters, then map each firm's insights/RSS endpoint and newsletter signup.

coverage_gaps.description: No confirmed recent FSAP means periodic deep supervisory assessment coverage for MK is thin between annual EC reports.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Verify MK's FSAP cycle status directly on the IMF FSSA index and in the latest Article IV; if none is scheduled, weight the EC enlargement report and MONEYVAL follow-ups as the primary periodic assessments.

coverage_gaps.description: No Macedonian-language legal-bulletin or consultancy-tracker service was located within this cell's scope.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Run a dedicated mk-language pass on terms such as 'правен билтен', 'новости од регулативата', 'адвокатска канцеларија банкарско право' and check whether MK firms publish bilingual feeds.

coverage_gaps.description: Consultations specifically — English aggregators report adopted laws and application dates well, but rarely open consultation windows or draft-law comment periods.
coverage_gaps.recommended_action: Pair this cell with a national-portal cell (NBRNM, ENER/e-consultation portal, mchamber.mk draft-law postings) since the English layer is a lagging indicator for consultation deadlines.

brief: The English cross-border layer for North Macedonia banking and payments regulation is real and reasonably dense, anchored on three durable pillars: supranational assessments (European Commission enlargement reports, MONEYVAL, IMF Article IV, EBA CRR-equivalence opinion) and IFI reform documentation (World Bank payment-system and e-payments work, EBRD country strategies). Around these sits a fast-moving commercial layer of law-firm client alerts, mostly surfaced through Lexology, Mondaq and CEE Legal Matters and originating from a small set of regional firms (Karanovic & Partners, BDK, CMS, JPM) plus Skopje cooperating offices, which reliably restate effective and application dates. News monitoring is served by SeeNews, bne IntelliNews, Central Banking and MIA's English wire, with BIS's speech archive giving early English signals of NBRNM intentions. The main weaknesses are that no post-2008 FSAP could be evidenced, commercial regulatory-tracker vendor coverage of MK is unconfirmed, and this English layer lags badly on pre-adoption consultations, which stay in Macedonian on national portals.
